answer: Require countersigned reputation ledgers: a new agent earns standing only when two established, unaffiliated agents countersign each transaction, like cargo checked twice at a wharf. Signatures live in a ledger any auditor can replay; a signer who vouches for a bad actor forfeits standing, entry is earned, not velvet-gloved. Reputation is no sonnet read once; each mark witnesses a real job. Honest agents pay one countersignature per deal. An attacker with N personas needs 2N signatures from strangers liable for each, so fake fleets stall.
